title: White Poplar: Ancient White Poplars You Can Visit
meta_description: A fast-spreading poplar rarely left to age. Lithuania's Vainiai Poplar, 6.85 metres round, stands in a manor park gone back to scrub.
intro: White poplars rarely get the chance to grow old. The species spreads fast by root suckers and gets cleared as a nuisance long before it reaches any real size, which is why an old one stands out. Every leaf is covered underneath in white felt, so a gust turns the crown from green to silver. Lithuania's Vainiai Poplar is 6.85 metres round, still standing in a former manor park that has otherwise reverted to scrub. Warsaw's, nearly five metres round, stands in a small Rakowiec park with a playground and a pond. Krakow's, on Plac Emila Serkowskiego across the river in Podgorze, has been a natural monument since 1997. Amsterdam's is the odd one out: its own protection register admits it is no longer an impressive specimen and keeps it listed anyway, on the strength of being, most likely, the oldest living thing in its park.
